To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have developed an unsupervised method to learn video representations using LSTMs and that these representations are helpful for supervised tasks like action recognition.

(i) LSTM networks can learn representations of video that are useful for supervised learning problems, (ii) these representations can generalize to longer temporal scales and to different domains, (iii) these representations can be learned from raw pixels without any human annotation, (iv) they can help in few-shot learning problems, and (v) the features can be visualized.
• We show that a model trained to predict the future can learn to represent video sequences.

learning representations for video sequences using LSTMs, and analyzing and interpreting these representations.
learning representations of visual sequences, and using them for different tasks, such that the representations are generalizable to different domains and time scales.
the question of how to learn video representations that can capture the temporal structure in videos, in a manner that is unsupervised, general, and scalable.
